title: Length-Controlled Comparison
hypothesis: At matched token counts, expert-depth contexts score higher than shallow contexts. The gap observed in exp_002 was a length artefact.
context_version: v3 (expert_short: same domains as expert but ~80 tokens, matched to shallow)
finding: expert_short (83 tok, 0.196) approximates shallow (61 tok, 0.217). Residual gap is 9.7%. log(n) ratio between 83 and 61 tokens predicts 7.5% suppression. Length accounts for the entire remaining gap. At truly matched token counts, expert_short ≈ shallow. SORC spectral entropy measures representational diversity, not relational depth. Expert paragraphs on one domain produce semantic clustering at deep layers (layers 20-32 score 0.07-0.15 vs 0.15-0.33 for shallow).
conclusion: Single-paragraph expert contexts are the wrong unit of analysis. ISC's mechanism operates over extended multi-turn conversation, not single paragraphs. Next experiment: multi-turn conversation fragments vs single-shot at matched token count.
